Definition: from G5259 and G4762; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively):--come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).
BiblicalUsage: The word hypostréphō carries the sense of to return, to turn back. In Luke 1:56, the text says "and returned to her own house." In Acts 1:12, the text says "Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet."
TheologicalSignificance: What hypostréphō teaches me is that repentance is not grovelling; it is turning around and walking the other way. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Conversion of Paul; Mary Visits Elizabeth
